Hudhaifa relates that twelve hypocrites of the Prophet's Ummah will be kept from Paradise, and says twelve of the people of Aqaba were enemies of Allah and His Messenger.
All who climbed the hill of Murar were pardoned except the owner of a red camel, who preferred finding his lost thing to the Prophet seeking forgiveness for him.
A scribe of the Prophet from Banu Najjar ran away to join the People of the Book; after his death the earth threw him out each time they buried him.
A gale blew at a hypocrite's death, two hypocrites face a fiercer fever on Resurrection Day, and a hypocrite is like a sheep straying between two flocks.
A bulky person on the Day of Judgement will not weigh as much as a gnat before Allah, as the verse says no balance will be set up for them.
A Jewish scholar says Allah will hold all creation on His fingers, the Prophet smiling agreement; on Judgement Day Allah will grip earth and heavens, saying: I am the Lord.
The Prophet lists what Allah created on each day of the week, from clay on Saturday to Adam after Asr on Friday, the last creation.
On the Day of Resurrection people gather on a white plain, stand on the Sirat when earth and heaven are changed, and the earth becomes one bread for Paradise's people.
The Prophet says that if ten Jewish scholars followed him, no Jew on earth would remain outside Islam.
When Jews asked the Prophet about the Soul he stayed silent until revelation came that the Soul is by his Lord's command and people are given little knowledge.
Al-As b. Wa'il will not pay Khabbab unless he denies Muhammad, saying he will pay once raised with his property and children, and a verse comes down.
Abu Jahl asks Allah for stones if the Prophet is true, and vows to trample the praying Prophet's neck but recoils from a ditch of fire; verses come down.
Ibn Mas'ud explains the Smoke as what starving Quraysh saw in the famine the Prophet invoked, one of five signs now past; Ubayy lists it among worldly punishments.
In the Prophet's lifetime the moon split in two, one part either side of the mountain at Mina, when Mecca's people asked for a sign, and he said: Bear witness.
None is more patient than Allah at hearing irksome things: people ascribe partners and a son to Him, yet He protects them and provides for them.
On Resurrection Day a disbeliever would give the earth's gold as ransom, though only not associating partners with Allah was asked of him, and disbelievers assemble on their faces.
Dipped once in the Fire, a denizen of Hell who lived in luxury will deny knowing comfort, and dipped once in Paradise, the world's most miserable will deny all hardship.
Allah rewards a believer's good deeds in this world and the Hereafter, while a disbeliever is repaid for his deeds in this world and finds none left in the Hereafter.
A believer is like a crop tossed by wind, a hypocrite or disbeliever like a cypress uprooted at once, and a Muslim like the date-palm, whose leaves do not wither.
Satan despairs of being worshipped in Arabia but sows discord, prizing most whoever splits spouses; everyone has a devil, but Allah keeps the Prophet safe from his.
No one, not even the Prophet, enters Paradise by deeds alone, only through Allah's Mercy, so act moderately, and the deed Allah loves most is the constant one.
The Prophet prayed until his feet swelled, and when told his earlier and later sins were pardoned, he asked whether he should not be a grateful servant.
Ibn Mas'ud preached once a week rather than daily, lest his listeners be bored, as the Prophet left days without sermons for the same reason.
Paradise is surrounded by hardships and the Fire by temptations.
Allah has prepared for His pious servants what no eye saw, no ear heard and no heart perceived, as the verse says no soul knows what is hidden for them.
In Paradise a rider cannot cross a tree's shade in a hundred years, and Allah tells its people He will grant them His pleasure and never be displeased with them.
Paradise's people will see those in the chambers above them like shining planets on the horizon, and believers who affirm the truth will reach the abodes of the Apostles.
The Prophet says those of his Ummah he loves most will come after him, each longing to see him even at the cost of family and wealth.
A street of Paradise visited each Friday adds beauty, and the first to enter have faces like the full moon, no bodily waste, musk sweat, gold combs and two wives.
Paradise's people eat and drink without waste, their food passing as belching and musk sweat; they praise Allah as they breathe and are promised lasting health, life, youth and plenty.
A believer in Paradise has a tent of one hollow pearl sixty miles wide; Saihan, Jaihan, Euphrates and Nile are among its rivers, and some enter with hearts like birds'.
Allah created Adam in His image, sixty cubits tall, and had him greet the angels, whose reply became his offspring's greeting, and all who enter Paradise will have his form.
Hell is dragged by seventy thousand bridles, earthly fire is a seventieth of it, a stone fell seventy years to its floor, and fire reaches people from ankles to collar-bones.
Hell claims the proud and Paradise the humble in their dispute; Allah calls them His punishment and His mercy, fills Hell by placing His foot, and creates others for Paradise.
Death, brought as a white ram, is slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, and both peoples are told they will live forever without death, to one's delight and the other's grief.
In Hell a disbeliever's molar will be like Uhud, his skin three nights' journey thick, and the span of his shoulders a swift rider's three-day journey.
Paradise's people are the meek and humble, whose oaths Allah fulfils even when they are driven from doors, and Hell's people are the haughty and proud.
In a sermon the Prophet recites the verse on the man who hamstrung the dromedary, then warns against flogging one's wife like a slave and laughing at breaking wind.
The Prophet saw Amr, named b. Luhayy or b. Amir, the first to devote animals to idols, dragging his intestines in the Fire; Ibn Musayyib explains the bahira and sa'iba.
Among Hell's people are those with whips like ox tails who flog people, living under Allah's wrath, and women clothed yet naked, misled and misleading, who will not smell Paradise.
